claims.text: Directional solidification will induce nanoscale lamellar structures in eutectic high-entropy alloys.
The induced nanoscale lamellar structure will contain alternating phases.
Controlled cooling rates can produce nanoscale lamellae during directional solidification.
The alloy composition must remain within the eutectic region for the intervention to work as proposed.
Nanoscale phase boundaries strengthen the alloy by impeding dislocation motion.
Interactions between alternating phases provide pathways for strain accommodation and thereby maintain ductility.
Directional solidification that produces nanoscale lamellae will significantly increase yield strength relative to a conventionally solidified homogeneous microstructure.
Directional solidification that produces nanoscale lamellae will significantly increase elongation to failure relative to a conventionally solidified homogeneous microstructure.
The simultaneous strength and ductility improvement is expected only for compositions that form stable eutectic structures.
The simultaneous improvement requires cooling conditions that create nanoscale lamellae without causing excessive brittleness.
